name: Single-admin private food-draft service/access boundary
phase: Specification only; implementation requires separate explicit authorization
objective: Define a dependency-injected single-admin private service over FOOD-001B/C, keeping access decisions outside ownership-neutral persistence and granting no public or sale authority.
reusableIdentityAuthorities: src/lib/identity/session/principal-resolver.ts: SessionPrincipalResolver contract and trusted principal-resolution pattern; no concrete session resolver construction or session wiring in this slice
accessModel: Explicitly single-admin only. Inject a repository, trusted caller resolver and exactly one permitted canonical administrator PrincipalId at service construction. Validate the injected administrator ID with parsePrincipalId; reject invalid configuration rather than defaulting or inferring it.

Do not hardcode River's ID. PrincipalId/parsePrincipalId are caller identity authority; names, food IDs, request payloads, River OS paths/session booleans and ownership claims are not authorization authority.
Possession of a food product/recipe ID never implies permission. The service adds no owner IDs to snapshots or repository contracts and no ownership registry.
Owner-scoped/multi-user access is deferred to a separately authorized tenant-isolation design. Caller identity is used only for the access decision.
authorizationOrder: On every operation resolve and authorize the trusted caller before operation-payload validation and before any repository read, write or list call.
Resolve fresh on every operation; never cache a prior successful decision across operations.
Unauthenticated, forbidden or unavailable access reveals no record-existence information and performs zero repository calls.

Validate successful resolution shape and canonical principal identity at runtime using parsePrincipalId. Malformed/noncanonical identity or malformed resolver output fails closed as access-unavailable without repository access.

A resolver unauthenticated outcome maps to unauthenticated; its unavailable outcome or thrown failure maps to access-unavailable. A valid resolved principal unequal to the injected administrator maps to forbidden. Never repair or normalize malformed identities.
operationRequirements: Wrap the existing FoodDraftRepository operations without changing their contract. Preserve supplied arguments exactly, including canonical IDs, versions, recipe references, expected predecessor, options, limits and cursors; preserve omitted optional arguments rather than fabricating replacements.

FOOD-001A remains domain-validation authority; FOOD-001B/C remain persistence/serialization authority. Delegate operation validation to those authorities after authorization, without normalization or repair.
Never generate identities/versions, merge revisions, retarget evidence, silently renumber, substitute latest recipe versions or reinterpret structural completeness.

Preserve detached frozen snapshots and unresolved/completeness semantics. Neither structural evidence nor reviewed findings grant approval, safety, eligibility, exemption, readiness or sale authority.
No direct D1 operations or binding selection; the injected repository may be the unchanged in-memory or D1 adapter.

requirements: Repository append outcomes created, already-present and conflict remain successful service values. Exact-read found/not-found and listing pages likewise remain successful values.
Do not turn expected conflict/not-found into authorization or storage errors. Preserve repository outcomes and their values unchanged.

FoodDraftValidationError from operation validation maps to invalid-input. FoodDraftStorageError and any unexpected repository exception map to storage; do not classify arbitrary failures by message text or leak raw exceptions.
Access failures preserve their distinct codes using fixed service messages. Never expose raw SQL, D1 errors, private evidence, stack traces or internal repository details through service errors.
Do not infer success after a thrown uncertain repository write; return storage and leave retry semantics to FOOD-001B/C.

auditAndOwnership: Durable audit/event storage is explicitly deferred. No actor IDs, timestamps, audit IDs, event records or audit writes in food snapshots or repositories.
No logging/event sink, clock, generated audit identity or other audit side effect is introduced. Caller identity exists only for access decisions.
tests: Missing identity/unauthenticated resolution denies access; wrong canonical principal returns forbidden; malformed/noncanonical identity and malformed resolver outputs fail closed as access-unavailable.
Resolver unavailable outcomes and thrown failures map to access-unavailable using fixed sanitized messages.
For all ten operations, denied callers cause zero repository reads/writes/lists; authorization precedes payload validation and discloses no record existence.
Authorization is independently resolved on every operation, including a successful decision followed by revocation, denial or resolver failure.
Payload-supplied principal/admin/role-like fields cannot grant access or substitute the trusted caller. Authorized malformed payloads remain subject to unchanged domain/repository validation.
Authorized operations preserve exact arguments, IDs, versions, recipe references, expected predecessors, optional argument omission, limits/cursors and repository outcomes.
Created, conflict, already-present, found/not-found, listing results, validation failure, storage failure and all access failures remain distinguishable.
Frozen snapshots and unresolved/completeness semantics remain unchanged; no result field or operation adds approval/readiness/sale authority.
Fixed messages do not leak SQL, repository details, stack traces or private evidence from resolver/repository exceptions.
Invalid injected administrator configuration is rejected; no hardcoded principal or authorization inference exists.

Source isolation permits food domain/repository authority and shared identity contracts only; no runtime bindings, routes, session wiring, River OS UI, audit side effects, commerce access or unrelated subsystem authority.
deferredScope: No River OS routes/UI integration, sessions/session wiring, runtime database binding selection, RIVER_FOOD_DB binding/configuration, database creation/provisioning or migration execution.
No public access/product exposure, commerce/checkout/Stripe, fulfillment, accounting, community/public counters, deployment or production data.
No insurance/Sesh/creator or unrelated subsystem changes. Reuse FOOD-001A/B/C unchanged and preserve existing additive directions and external readiness gates.
currentTaskBoundary: Create only this specification; do not implement, modify existing source, stage, commit, migrate, configure runtime access or deploy.
nextStep: Review this specification before separately authorizing the two-file private service/access implementation.
